name: Kafka Trigger
category_description: Trigger node - starts a workflow when an event happens
description: Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform that one can use for high-performance data pipelines, streaming analytics, data integration, and mission-critical applications

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: Name of the queue of topic to consume from

parameters.name: resolveOffset

options.name: On Execution Completion
options.description: Resolve offset after execution completion regardless of the status

options.name: On Execution Success
options.description: Resolve offset only if execution status equals success

options.name: On Allowed Execution Statuses
options.description: Resolve offset only if execution status in the list of selected statuses

options.name: Immediately
options.description: Resolve offset immediately after message received. This option is not recommended as it can cause messages loss.

parameters.description: Select on which condition the offsets should be resolved. In the manual mode, when execution started by clicking on Execute Workflow or Execute Step button, offsets are always resolved immediately after message received.

parameters.name: useSchemaRegistry
parameters.description: Whether to use Confluent Schema Registry

options.name: allowAutoTopicCreation
options.description: Whether to allow sending message to a previously non-existing topic

options.name: autoCommitThreshold
options.description: The consumer will commit offsets after resolving a given number of messages

options.name: autoCommitInterval
options.description: The consumer will commit offsets after a given period, for example, five seconds

options.name: batchSize
options.description: Number of messages to process in each batch, when set to 1, message-by-message processing is enabled

options.name: eachBatchAutoResolve
options.description: Whether to auto resolve offsets for each batch

options.name: fetchMaxBytes
options.description: Maximum amount of data the server should return for a fetch request. In bytes. Default is 1MB. Higher values allow fetching more messages at once.

options.name: fetchMinBytes
options.description: Minimum amount of data the server should return for a fetch request. In bytes. Server will wait up to fetchMaxWaitTime for this amount to accumulate.

options.name: heartbeatInterval
options.description: Controls how often the consumer sends heartbeats to the broker to indicate it is still alive. Must be lower than Session Timeout. Recommended value is approxima

options.name: heartbeatInterval
options.description: Heartbeats are used to ensure that the consumer's session stays active

options.name: maxInFlightRequests
options.description: The maximum number of unacknowledged requests the client will send on a single connection

options.name: fromBeginning
options.description: Whether to read message from beginning

options.name: jsonParseMessage
options.description: Whether to try to parse the message to an object

options.name: keepBinaryData
options.description: Whether to keep message value as binary data for downstream processing (e.g., Avro deserialization)

options.name: parallelProcessing
options.description: Whether to process messages in parallel resolving offsets independently or in order resolving offsets after execution completion. In the manual mode, when execu

options.name: partitionsConsumedConcurrently
options.description: Number of Kafka partitions to process in parallel. Controls how many partitions are processed concurrently by the consumer.

options.name: onlyMessage
options.description: Whether to return only the message property

options.name: returnHeaders
options.description: Whether to return the headers received from Kafka

options.name: rebalanceTimeout
options.description: The maximum time allowed for a consumer to join the group

options.name: errorRetryDelay
options.description: Delay in milliseconds before retrying after a failed offset resolution. This prevents rapid retry loops that could overwhelm the Kafka broker.
